To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
in fully adapted fish the rates of synthesis and release of prolactin are inversely proportional to external salinity.

the rates of PRL synthesis and PRL secretion are inversely correlated to environmental salinity in P. latipinna, that these rates are temporarily unbalanced following a transfer between salinities, and that PRL granule size in these cells is inversely correlated to external salinity.

in the killifish the prolactin cell responds to changes in salinity in a manner that is quantitatively related to the magnitude of the change, and that the response is mediated by changes in prolactin cell secretory activity and by changes in the morphology of the cells that surround the prolactin secreting cells.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the regulation of prolactin secretion in a teleost (Poecilia) and its relationship to external salinity.
the regulation of prolactin secretion in the teleost fish, Poecilia latpinna, in relation to the external salinity.
prolactin secretion in a teleost (Poecilia) adapted to various salinities and the changes in the ultrastructure of the prolactin secreting cell that occur during these adaptations.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the prolactin cell of Poecilia is an extremely sensitive indicator of the external salinity and is capable of rapid adjustments in its synthetic and release rates in accordance with the external salinity.
the PRL cells of P. latipinna respond to changes in salinity by a complex series of coordinated and uncoordinated alterations in the rates of synthesis, release and removal of PRL.
the ultrastructural changes in the prolactin secreting cells are directly correlated with the changes in prolactin release rate.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

in teleost fish, PRL cells are capable of responding rapidly and quantitatively to changes in environmental salinity, and that the secretory activity and the metabolic state of the PRL cell are closely related to the external salinity.

in the teleost fish PRL cells are exquisitely sensitive to external salinity and to rapid changes therein, and are able to respond to such changes with a variety of adjustments in their synthetic, secretory and degradative activities, and with a variety of morphological changes in the cell.

the PRL cells of P. latipinna are capable of responding to changes in environmental salinity by adjusting their secretory activity to the external medium, and that the rate of PRL synthesis adjusts to the rate of release with a lag of 30-72 h, depending on the direction of the change in salinity.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the PRL cells in P. latipinna have the capacity to adapt to a new external salinity, and that this adaptation involves changes in both the rate of PRL synthesis and the rate of P RL release.
the prolactin cell is not just a passive storage organ for the hormone.
the prolactin cell is a dynamic cell type, with its secretory activity and morphology being responsive to environmental salinity.
